title: Active, passive or neutral: mode follows the evaluation

D0.outcome: Explains that the right kind of game follows the valuation: better, play actively; worse, defend and restore freedom; equal, manoeuvre.

D1.outcome: Labels a position better, worse or equal and chooses the mode with a reason.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, picks the move that fits the mode, and does not attack from a clearly worse position or sit still when clearly better.

D3.outcome: Handles exceptions: counter-attack from a worse position; rejects the source's advice to give up when hopelessly worse.

conditions: An honest valuation exists first (the hard part).
contrasts: Playing actively from an inferior position is the most dangerous choice, yet counter-attack remains the normal way out.
Playing passively from a superior position is the most wasteful.
A dead-equal position with no clear plan on either side.

soft_prereq_notes.ATK.PACE.D1: mode and pace of an attack are linked
